blocks.content: kubectl rollout is a family of subcommands for managing a Deployment's rollout lifecycle, most already covered in the Deployments module, plus one more worth knowing: restart.
rollout is not one command, it is a namespace for several related ones: status, history, undo, and restart, each managing a different aspect of a Deployment's ongoing lifecycle.

blocks.alt: One command family, several related subcommands underneath it

blocks.content: rollout status, rollout history, and rollout undo are covered in full depth already, in the Rolling Updates, Revision History, and Rollback topics of the Deployments module, exactly the same commands, this is a quick recap, not new ground.

blocks.alt: Already covered fully, this is a recap, not new material

blocks.content: rollout restart triggers a rolling restart of every Pod, using exactly the rolling update mechanism covered in the Deployments module, but without changing the image or any other spec field at all.

blocks.alt: The same rolling mechanism, triggered deliberately, with no actual spec change

blocks.text: 4. Why You Would Actually Want This

blocks.content: This connects directly to a real limitation covered in the Configuration module's Volume Configuration topic, a mounted ConfigMap can update live, but the application still has to notice and reload it. rollout restart is the practical, brute-force way to force every Pod to pick up a changed ConfigMap or Secret, by simply restarting them all.

blocks.alt: The practical fix for exactly the limitation covered in the Configuration module

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: rollout is a family of subcommands, status, history, and undo are covered fully in the Deployments module, restart is the one genuinely new addition here.
rollout restart forces every Pod through a rolling restart with no spec change at all, the practical way to make Pods pick up a changed ConfigMap or Secret.
